How to import data

```{r}
load("data/fusarium.Rdata")
```

We are checking for Effect of the pathogen on celery (both varieties each) and then pairwise test to prove that they have similar susceptibility effect of the pathogen on parsley (both varieties each)

1.  First Shapiro Wilk to check residuals
2.  t-test to compare celery varieties susceptibility
3.  ANOVA for parsley-italien, parsley-curly, & both celery varieties (i.e. if celery similar susceptibility) one anova for each

we will check the final height, total weight and discoloration

Shapiro-Wilk WEIGHT

```{r}
F1$Block <- factor(F1$Block)
F1$Total_weight <- as.numeric(F1$Total_weight)


w_italian <- lm(Total_weight ~ Treatment, data = subset(F1, Variety == "Italian"))
w_curly   <- lm(Total_weight ~ Treatment, data = subset(F1, Variety == "Curly"))
w_c26 <- lm(Total_weight ~ Treatment, data = subset(F1, Variety == "C26"))
w_c42 <- lm(Total_weight ~ Treatment, data = subset(F1, Variety == "C42"))
# Total_weight ~ Treatment + Block = total weight depends on whether the plant was inoculated (Treatment) and which greenhouse block it was in (Block)



# Shapiro-Wilk on the residuals
shapiro.test(residuals(w_italian))
# p = 0.004515
shapiro.test(residuals(w_curly))
# p-value = 0.006208
shapiro.test(residuals(w_c26))
# p-value = 0.6798
shapiro.test(residuals(w_c42))
# p-value = 0.394

## -> parsley not normally distributed (no ANOVA)
## -> clery normally distributed -> ANOVA possible

# Beim Shapiro-Wilk-Test lautet die Nullhypothese „die Residuen sind normalverteilt“. Ist p > 0,05, wird sie nicht abgelehnt und die Annahme gilt als erfüllt. Ist p < 0,05, sind die Residuen signifikant nicht normalverteilt


```

ANOVA for celery

```{r}

anova(m_c26)
# p-value = 2.196e-09 *** (< 0.05)
# So inoculated and control C26 plants differ significantly in total weight
anova(m_c42)
# p-value = <2e-16 *** (< 0.05)
# So inoculated and control C42 plants differ significantly in total weight


```

LAJANDAS PLOTS
## Analysissssssssssssssssss

```{r}
load("data/fusarium.Rdata")
summary(F1)

#Change the columns with charater variables to categorical variables
F1$Plant <- as.factor(F1$Plant)
F1$Variety <- as.factor(F1$Variety)
F1$Treatment <- as.factor(F1$Treatment)
F1$Block <- as.factor(F1$Block)
F1$PlantVar <- as.factor(F1$PlantVar)
F1$PlantVarTreat <- as.factor(F1$PlantVarTreat)

str(F1)


```


Plant height

```{r}


# mean plant height
by(F1$height_final, F1$PlantVarTreat, mean, na.rm = TRUE)

# SD
by(F1$height_final, F1$PlantVarTreat, sd, na.rm = TRUE)


model_height <- aov(height_final ~ PlantVarTreat + Block, data = F1)

summary(model_height)


TukeyHSD(model_height)


# fix the order of the groups
lvls <- c("Celery_C26_Control",    "Celery_C26_KX31-inoculated",
          "Celery_C42_Control",    "Celery_C42_KX31-inoculated",
          "Parsley_Curly_Control", "Parsley_Curly_KX31-inoculated",
          "Parsley_Italian_Control","Parsley_Italian_KX31-inoculated")
F1$PlantVarTreat <- factor(F1$PlantVarTreat, levels = lvls)

# one colour per variety: light = control, dark = inoculated
cols <- c("#a6cee3", "#1f78b4",   # C26
          "darkolivegreen3", "forestgreen",   # C42
          "burlywood2", "darkorange",   # Curly
          "thistle", "darkorchid2")   # Italian

# box positions: pairs close together, gaps between varieties
pos <- c(1, 2,  3.5, 4.5,  6.5, 7.5,  9, 10)

par(mar = c(5, 4, 4, 9))   # extra space on the right for the legend

boxplot(height_final ~ PlantVarTreat, data = F1,
        at = pos, col = cols,
        xaxt = "n", xlab = "",
        ylab = "Plant height (cm)",
        main = "Plant height by variety and treatment")

# variety names under each pair
axis(1, at = c(1.5, 4, 7, 9.5), labels = c("C26", "C42", "Curly", "Italian"), tick = FALSE)

# crop names below
mtext(c("Celery", "Parsley"), side = 1, line = 3, at = c(2.75, 8.25), font = 2)

# dashed line between celery and parsley
abline(v = 5.5, lty = 2, col = "grey60")

# legend outside the plot on the right
legend("topright", inset = c(-0.28, 0), xpd = TRUE, bty = "n",
       title = "Treatment",
       legend = c("Control (light)", "KX31-inoculated (dark)"),
       fill = c("grey85", "grey35"))
colors()

plot(model_height)

```






Total Weight

```{r}
by(F1$Total_weight, F1$PlantVarTreat, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
by(F1$Total_weight, F1$PlantVarTreat, sd, na.rm = TRUE)

boxplot(Total_weight ~ PlantVarTreat, data = F1,
        las = 2,
        cex.axis = 0.7,
        ylab = "Total weight",
        xlab = "Variety and treatment",
        main = "Total plant weight by variety and treatment")

model_weight <- aov(Total_weight ~ PlantVarTreat + Block, data = F1)

summary(model_weight)

TukeyHSD(model_weight, "PlantVarTreat")

plot(model_weight)
```

Total plant weight is different among the eight variety-treatment combinations ANOVA \< 0.001). Block had no significant effect p = 0.356.
